Gallery curation then chooses a diverse set of wallpapers out of the candidate pool.
provenance: builder.overview:pipeline — three stages down the sheet, 1344 wide on the site's well. Every location on it is a seat of a recorded tentative gallery, named on this row by its own `<stamp>|<recipe key>` and resolved from artifacts/curation/tentative/<stamp>/gallery.jsonl for the seat and the candidate ledger for the recipe. Stamp 20260902T161757Z.

Stage 1, three locations at 432x243: each drawn fresh through the engine at that size, supersample 3, mode smooth, colormap twilight_shifted, cap from the depth-aware policy, no crop — the neutral map every figure that is not about colour uses, because what the stage is showing is the geometry the walk found rather than any coloring of it. Panels in reading order.

Stage 2, 4 colorings of a693d6c7's own frame at 321x181: rendered fresh at 1280x720, supersample 3, and fitted. Everything but the palette is held at that recipe's own pass — mode smooth, curve linear, cap 34593; palette gamma 1, cycles 1, phase 0, reverse false, transfer value, rolloff none — so the only thing changing across the row is the colour. The marked panel is the map the run kept; the other three were a uniform draw without replacement from the **authored** maps of the pool a colorize may pick between, data/palette_choice/pool.json — the maps written against the palette prompt rather than extracted from a picture or converted from an upstream library — random.Random(20260902).sample. Not a neighbourhood of the kept map, so the row shows the spread a colorize is choosing out of. The three are written down in the maker rather than re-drawn at draw time, because the pool grows and a re-run would recolour a committed figure. In reading order: palette `cmr.prinsenvlag`; palette `Green, Gold, Magenta`; palette `Sulphur & Plum`; palette `Mist Field, Ink Well`. No name is drawn on the row: a map's name tells a reader nothing the gradient under the panel does not, and four of them turn a band of colour into a band of text.

Mirror follows the map here rather than being held at the kept recipe's flag: `colorize.py` sets it as `colormap not in self.cyclic` and this row does the same, so a cyclic map arrives unfolded and the engine is never asked to halve a cycle. That is also why a cyclic map is no longer dropped from the draw, which it used to be — holding the flag fixed was the thing that made it impossible, and every authored map is cyclic. The flags are derived from the library and held to this row's own record, so a map changing kind next door is a refusal rather than a quiet redraw. Folded here: `cmr.prinsenvlag` true; `Green, Gold, Magenta` false; `Sulphur & Plum` false; `Mist Field, Ink Well` false.

Every panel of this row is autolevelled, because an attempt is not finished at the render: the operator measures the picture's tone and, where it sits outside the band, pushes a curve through the map's own stops and draws again. The marked panel replays the run's own stamp, which is what makes it the same picture as the one in stage 3 rather than a shade lighter; the other three exist only in this figure, have no run and no stamp behind them, and are measured here by `autolevel.derive_curve` and drawn through `curved_stops` — the operator acting, not a second reading of something it already did.

Stage 3, three seats of the same recorded gallery at 432x243: each rendered fresh through the engine at 1280x720, supersample 3, and fitted. Nothing about the coloring is this figure's choice — mode, mode settings, curve, map, the whole palette pass and the cap all come off the ledger's recipe.

Autolevel: every candidate behind these seats was made with band_autolevel/v1 switched on. A ledger recipe keeps only the reduced stamp of that — the operator, the switch and the band's sha256 — so the curve is read from the run's own record instead, depth/overnight_b_main, reframe_draw/q4_1h. The operator acted on a693d6c7 (black point 0.5953, white point 0.9819), and those panels were drawn through the stops that curve rebuilds — the wallpaper project's own `stops_from_stamp` replaying its own curve, never a second one measured here. It left the rest exactly alone, and those are the engine's own render. Held to that: each pick redrawn at the candidate's own 640x360 supersample 2 reproduces the stored picture its seat points at to mean absolute difference 3.0-5.5 of 255, codec floor 1.4-2.8, and `builder check`'s `seats` is what keeps it true.

caption: The parameter and dynamical planes the project draws. The Mandelbrot and degree-3, 4, 5, and 6 multibrot parameter planes are each shown whole with two marked values of c, followed by the Julia renderings those two values produce, each framed in the color of the mark it belongs to. Phoenix is already a dynamical-plane family, so the last three show the celebrated Ushiki constants first and then two other parameter choices.

facts.claim: The Mandelbrot panel is shown whole at centre -0.77, width 4.4 because the filled set was measured to reach re = 0.4525 — well right of the main cardioid's cusp at 0.375.
facts.source: fractal-wallpapers engine/src/family.rs, Family::measured_extent — Multibrot{degree:2} => re (-2.0, 0.4525), im (-1.1, 1.1), and the doc table above it deriving the (-0.77, 0) w 4.4 home view from it

provenance: builder.families:family_planes — eighteen panels at 640x360, three to a row and landed one file a panel, this figure being split rather than composited: a family's whole-set view with two marked points on it, then a finished wallpaper of the Julia set each mark produces. The five whole-set views are the engine's own derived home views, rendered at supersample 3, mode smooth, in the map named on each line. The ten Julia panels are seats Matt picked by alias on 2026-09-25 (escape_families_ckpt148), two to a degree, each alias checked to be a unique prefix among the seats of the twenty-one recorded galleries and to sit on its row's plane. They are named on this row as <stamp>|<recipe key> and resolved from article/figure-recipes.jsonl, which holds the seat row and the ledger recipe for each; each is rendered fresh through the engine at 1280x720, supersample 3, and fitted to the panel. Nothing about their coloring is this figure's choice — mode, mode settings, curve, map, palette pass and cap all come off the ledger's recipe, so the mode changes from panel to panel with the picks and each panel's own line names it. The first of a row's two picks is the cyan mark and the second the rose. The Phoenix row is unchanged: two label-store rows scored 4 by hand, drawn the way a Julia set is, because that family has no parameter plane to mark.

Autolevel: every candidate behind these seats was made with band_autolevel/v1 switched on. A ledger recipe keeps only the reduced stamp of that — the operator, the switch and the band's sha256 — so the curve is read from the run's own record instead, depth/ame_b2_deep, depth/d6o_c2_deep, depth/fss125_recolour, depth/night_b, depth/smooth500_leg, hunt/d6s_open_a (re-measured here on 2026-09-25), rotation/ckpt120, rotation/ckpt120 (re-measured here on 2026-09-25), rotation/owed_ckpt121. It acted on 92c615d0 (black point 0.1476, white point 0.9672), 4438b8c4 (black point 0.0000, white point 0.8335), whose run recorded the fact and not the curve, so that curve is the operator's own rule measured again here, on the recipe drawn at its regime through the unlevelled map, and kept in article/figure-recipes.jsonl as `tone`. Those panels are drawn through it and linked with it, and each line gives how far the result is from the picture the gallery ships. It left the rest exactly alone, and those are the engine's own render. alt: Animated: three starting points advancing in step across the complex plane, one escaping fast, one bounded, one lingering near the boundary, with a |z|-versus-step chart alongside.
caption: Three orbits under the same quadratic rule, stepping together. One is past |z| = 2 within a few steps and gone for good, one stays bounded forever, and one hangs near the boundary for dozens of steps before it escapes. For the escaping tracks, the step where a track crosses the line on the chart is that orbit's escape time.
provenance: Drawn, not rendered: `python -m builder diagram escape-orbit-race`, from builder/diagrams.py. A 41-frame APNG at 960x540 (drawn at scale 2, 130 ms a frame, 1600 ms hold), plotting z <- z^2 + c from z = 0 over 40 steps at |z| > 2 for three constants: c = 0.5 + 0.5i (escapes at step 5), c = -0.075 + 0.655i (escapes at step 35), and c = -0.12256116687665 + 0.74486176661974i (never escapes). Plane panel spans +/-2.45 on both axes; the chart's ceiling is |z| = 2.5. No engine render.

alt: One Julia location under a cyclic amber palette at one, two, three, and four sweeps of the gradient, each panel over a strip of the gradient repeated as many times as that panel spends it.
caption: One location and one cyclic palette, swept across the frame's range k times. At k = 1 the gradient is spent once over a range most of the frame does not occupy, and wide areas come out nearly flat; each further sweep spends it again and pulls more of the structure apart. Repetition is the classic escape from a squeezed range, and it is why so many older Mandelbrot renders are striped with rings.
provenance: builder.fundamentals:cyclic_repeats — four panels at 640x360, supersample 3, one location and one cyclic palette swept k times. The frame is candidate ledger key 0daf678f61143941, seat 336 of the recorded tentative gallery 20260902T161757Z: the location as it ships, addressed by its own key rather than by a position in anything. The **map is this figure's own** and not that seat's *(Matt, 2026-09-02)*: Ember Gradient, an authored map, replacing the extracted nova-25 the seat ships with. It is the same map the second column of `render-discrete-and-smooth` is drawn in, which is the one place this page repeats a palette and is Matt's own call: the two figures are four screens apart and the one a reader has already met is the one that teaches what a ramp is. nova-25 closes by *mirroring* — colour(t) equals colour(1-t) exactly, measured 0.000 — so one sweep of it is already two mirrored halves and k sweeps read as 2k bands, which is the one thing this figure must not do. An authored map closes by travelling a loop instead: 90% of the library's extracted maps are palindromes and not one of its 375 authored maps is, while every map the library calls cyclic closes exactly, so the seam a repeat could show is never the thing being traded away. Nothing replays the ledger's own cap of 6,698 — the panels are drawn at the engine's depth policy, which answers the same number at this frame. Under each panel, 6px below it and 26px tall, the gradient as that panel spends it: `fractal-wallpapers palettes strip` for the map at width 640/k, laid down k times across the panel's width. The strip command takes no cycle count, so the repeat is composed from k engine-drawn ramps rather than one stretched — the map is cyclic and so drawn unfolded, which is the mirror false the renders above carry.

caption: Every rendering mode the pipeline draws from when searching for wallpaper candidates at each location.
provenance: builder.picks — every panel is a seat of a recorded tentative gallery, named on this row by its own `<stamp>|<recipe key>` and resolved from artifacts/curation/tentative/<stamp>/gallery.jsonl for the seat and the candidate ledger for the recipe. Rendered fresh through the engine at 1280x720, supersample 3, then fitted to 314x177 and landed one file a panel, this figure being split rather than composited; the stored 640x360 thumbnail a seat points at is the picture the judges were shown and is not a source here. Nothing about the coloring is this figure's choice: mode, mode settings, curve, map, the whole palette pass and the cap all come off the ledger's recipe. Stamps 20260904T233233Z, 20260906T133559Z, 20260908T211552Z; panels in reading order, 4 across.

Autolevel: every candidate behind these seats was made with band_autolevel/v1 switched on. A ledger recipe keeps only the reduced stamp of that — the operator, the switch and the band's sha256 — so the curve is read from the run's own record instead, depth/breadth_strange, depth/mine_diverse_0903_b1, depth/mine_diverse_0903_d2, depth/night_b, depth/overnight_a_main, depth/rare_a, depth/sm_direct, reframe_draw/q4_1h, runs/gallery2, runs/gallery3. It acted on none of them, which by that operator's rule means it returned each base render untouched, so every panel here is the engine's own render of the recipe. Held to that: each pick redrawn at the candidate's own 640x360 supersample 2 reproduces the stored picture its seat points at to mean absolute difference 3.0-5.5 of 255, codec floor 1.4-2.8, and `builder check`'s `seats` is what keeps it true.

Which seat stands for a mode is a uniform random draw over that mode's q4 seats of the stamp — scratch/modes/repick_gallery.py, seed 20260905 — rejecting any seat standing on a location another figure already stands on, and any whose run recorded that the autolevel operator acted without recording the curve it acted with. A q4 seat is one over P(>=4) 0.50, the render judge's own cutpoint and the bar the solve seats on; the stamp filled all thousand of its seats and every one of them clears it, so the bar refused nothing here and is stated because a later stamp's might. Nothing the draw seated was chosen for how it looks: the figure's claim is that the roster draws wallpapers, and a machine pick is what makes that claim.

Three of the thirteen are not the draw's — stripe, curvature and closest trap angle over smooth, which Matt replaced by hand on 2026-09-08, naming each by the alias under its tile on the curation browser. Each stands on a later stamp than the draw did, which is why this row names more than one, and each is a claim about the picker in the way the other ten are not.

A seat's mode is read off the ledger recipe and never off the seat row, the two having disagreed on eighteen seats of an earlier stamp — every one seated as smooth and recipe'd as itinerary — and the recipe being what the engine is handed.

provenance: builder.picks:minibrot_examples — six panels, three across and two down, landed one file a panel, this figure being split rather than composited. Every picture is rendered fresh through the engine at 1280x720, supersample 3, and fitted to 422x237. The bottom row's seats are named on this row as <stamp>|<recipe key> and resolved from article/figure-recipes.jsonl, and nothing about their coloring is this figure's choice: mode, mode settings, curve, map, palette pass and cap all come off the ledger's recipe. The ring on each top panel is drawn in after the fit, radius 13 in the first mark ink over a dark under-stroke, at the centre of the frame below as the panel's own geometry places it.

Autolevel: every candidate behind these seats was made with band_autolevel/v1 switched on. A ledger recipe keeps only the reduced stamp of that — the operator, the switch and the band's sha256 — so the curve is read from the run's own record instead, depth/on125_recolour1, rotation/ckpt120. It acted on none of them, which by that operator's rule means it returned each base render untouched, so every panel here is the engine's own render of the recipe. Held to that: each pick redrawn at the candidate's own 640x360 supersample 2 reproduces the stored picture its seat points at to mean absolute difference 3.0-5.5 of 255, codec floor 1.4-2.8, and `builder check`'s `seats` is what keeps it true.

alt: Three bar charts of how deep each root's walk got, beside three bars of how many roots produced a find at all.
caption: Left, how deep each root's walk got, in rungs below the root; right, the share of roots that admitted at least one frame. The top two rows are the two kinds of root in one run, and the third is a different run, shown for scale.
provenance: No render: a chart, drawn from two walk ledgers. A root counts once, and only if the run ever expanded it; depth is the deepest rung any candidate under it reached, and a root 'produced a find' if any candidate under it was admitted. Bars are shares of each arm's own roots, so arms of different sizes are comparable; the two demo arms ran in one run, under one frontier, competing for the same expansion budget.
Seeded roots (placed at locations a human rated a keeper): 132 roots, median depth 6, deepest 10, 130 admitting (98.5%); depth histogram 2:5, 3:6, 4:4, 5:30, 6:39, 7:29, 8:14, 9:4, 10:1.

Another run entirely (for scale — the same limits, a different root mix): 455 roots, median depth 6, deepest 13, 186 admitting (40.9%); depth histogram 2:166, 3:16, 4:6, 5:24, 6:67, 7:109, 8:23, 9:26, 10:8, 11:4, 12:5, 13:1.

alt: Four frames from one fractal family, in score order, each labeled with the decision its score buys: refused, expandable, a find, and an exceptional find.

caption: The three parts, and what each hands to the next. The top band is sixteen places the search admitted, all drawn in one neutral map because nothing about their color is settled yet. The middle band takes the marked one: two of its best results in different rendering modes, and two in different colors. The bottom band is eight seats from a curated gallery, chosen out of the pool.
provenance: builder.pool — three bands on one sheet 1316 wide, read top to bottom, each under its own title and with a plain arrow down the centre line between each pair of them. Sixteen panels at 151x85, 8 across; five at 248x140; eight at 314x177, 4 across. The titles are Finding good locations, Mining for wallpapers, Gallery curation — the sections either side of this one and this page's own word for what it does, so a reader who has met the contents rail has met all three. They are set 4 points above the label under a middle-band tile rather than below it: a title says what the whole block under it is and a label names one picture inside that block, so the smaller title the other headed sheets of this page still carry has the two ranks the wrong way round. The marked location wears the same amber frame in the first band and the second, and that frame is the only thing on the sheet saying the two are one place. Nothing on it is a count.

Band 2 — five tiles, every one of them at mandelbrot_sourcing/walk.jsonl node 308, panel 9 of the band above. The first is that location drawn exactly as band 1 draws it and at 248x140 instead of 151x85, wearing the same mark. The other four are candidates of the pool at that same frame, addressed by recipe key against artifacts/curation/candidate_ledger/rows.jsonl and drawn through the engine at 1280x720, supersample 3, then fitted to the tile. Nothing about the coloring is this figure's choice: mode, mode settings, curve, map, the whole palette pass and the cap all come off the ledger's recipe. Panels in reading order — the mode pair, then the color pair. The color pair's two tiles are labelled best blue color and best orange color, and the word in each is that candidate's own dominant hue family off the ledger's colour reading rather than a reading taken here.

Which four wallpapers stand for the mine is a search over every candidate the ledger holds at that exact frame and location, unreframed and not rejected, ranked on P(>=4) from the fine head's reading of the pool (gallery_grade_head/pool_scores.jsonl); a candidate that head has not read, whose run keeps no record this maker reads its autolevel stamp from, or on which the operator acted without its run recording the curve, is not in the search. Re-picked on 2026-09-16, when the ledger no longer held three of the four it had chosen, and solved again whole rather than around the one that survived, because that one was the weakest by far. The mode pair is two results that differ in rendering mode; the color pair is two that differ in dominant hue family, and holding that pair's mode fixed is preferred over letting it vary. Three rules bind the search: the four are four distinct pictures in four distinct maps, so the strongest result cannot stand in both pairs; each of them redraws to inside the tolerance `check`'s `seats` allows of the picture its own run shipped; and what is maximized is the weakest of the four rather than their sum, because the band's claim is that there is nothing mediocre in it.

Autolevel: every candidate behind these seats was made with band_autolevel/v1 switched on. A ledger recipe keeps only the reduced stamp of that — the operator, the switch and the band's sha256 — so the curve is read from the run's own record instead, depth/easy125_recolour, depth/fss125_recolour, runs/gallery4. It acted on none of them, which by that operator's rule means it returned each base render untouched, so every panel here is the engine's own render of the recipe. Held to that: each pick redrawn at the candidate's own 640x360 supersample 2 reproduces the stored picture its seat points at to mean absolute difference 3.0-5.5 of 255, codec floor 1.4-2.8, and `builder check`'s `seats` is what keeps it true.

What that redraw is worth, measured rather than asserted: every attempt of this visit that still has a stored picture was redrawn as well and compared with it, and the two differ by a mean absolute 3.13 of 255 over the frame, 4.13 at the worst of them. The outline on a panel is what the candidate ledger holds today, and the panels of a band are in the order of the fitted rank this run recorded — which is the ranking retention was applied against, and the one that stands now.

alt: Twenty-four wallpapers in a grid of six across and four down, in the order the gallery judge ranks them.
caption: The 24 pictures the gallery judge scores highest, in order, with no curation rule applied. All 24 score within 0.02 of one another. One palette colors a quarter of them, they come from only 20 places, and six pairs are near-twins. The real 1,000-picture gallery keeps just 12.
provenance: builder.picks — every panel is a candidate of the curation pool, never seated by anything this figure asked, named on this row as `candidate|<recipe key>` and resolved from article/figure-recipes.jsonl, which holds the candidate ledger's row for it. Rendered fresh through the engine at 1280x720, supersample 3, then fitted to 205x115 and landed one file a panel. Nothing about the coloring is this figure's choice: mode, mode settings, curve, map, the whole palette pass and the cap all come off the ledger's recipe. Panels in rank order, 6 across.

Tone: every candidate here was made with band_autolevel/v1 switched on. Each panel's curve is read from its run's own record where this module reads that kind of run (depth, hunt, mine, reframe_draw, remode, runs), and otherwise from the wallpaper project's own reader, `curation.stamps.for_rows` over the backfill overlay, which is where a rotation or a label-migration row is answered. Replayed through the curve the record keeps: 752e3977. Untouched, the engine's own render: 18. Copied as the stored 640x360 supersample 2 picture the judge scored, and carrying no explorer link, because no record holds a curve for them and a render of the recipe is not known to be the picture: eb3cd229, 84d01725, 5a9441eb, c4fae758, ba1b5cbc. A depth run records that the operator acted and drops the coefficients; a rotation run before 2026-09-16 recorded neither, and where the backfill has no row for one, nothing says whether the operator acted.

Which twenty-four: the pool `final139_general` was solved over, taken the way the solve takes it and read on 2026-09-25 against the live ledger — `curation.solve.pool()` (518,436 candidates after the mode policy, the human rejections and vetoes), then `solve.at_fine_bar` at that record's own `config.fine_bar` of 0.030242 on the gallery judge's column (19,197 candidates over 8,940 places, the record's own counts to the row), then `headroom.clearing` under each mode's own bar (19,197, a no-op on this pool). Every row of that ranked by p_fine, the fine head's P(>=4) as the k=3 `twelve_sheets_drop_high_asymmetric_auc_ge4_more_k3` ensemble mean reads it, descending, ties by recipe key, and the first twenty-four taken. No curation rule was applied: no neutral pre-selection, no one seat per place or cluster, no twin test, no mode, palette-group, spiral or colour cap. The twenty-fifth reads 0.978604.

alt: Three pairs of wallpapers, one pair to a row, each pair labeled with the distance between them: the first refused as near-duplicates, the second seated with the smallest distance in the gallery, and the third two ordinary wallpapers.
caption: Three pairs at increasing distance under the twin measure. The first is two pictures deemed far too close; only one is allowed into the gallery. The second is the closest pair the finished gallery holds, so it's deemed just different enough to be allowed. The third is what two ordinary wallpapers measure.
provenance: builder.curation:gallery_twins — six pictures and three numbers. Every panel is **the pass's own finished picture, copied**: the twin measure is taken on the 640x360 render a run wrote, so a redraw at any other regime would be a picture the number under it was never measured on. Nothing here reaches the engine.

The pass: tentative gallery 20260902T164622Z, solve leg tentative_n1000, taken at 2026-09-02T16:46:26Z against wallpapers commit a4157d705e67. It asked for 1,000 seats and filled 912. The pool it chose over carries stamp 553620ebc81a7e97, which is the same pool the earlier pass of that day was chosen over.

The measure: pixel-cloud sliced Wasserstein-1 between two finished pictures, over 256 directions, threshold 0.03809 out of ceiling.TAU, refusing a picture with 1 seated neighbour inside it. Every distance below was measured here through fractal_wallpapers.palettes.pixel_clouds, which is the module the pass measures with, and the refused pair is held to the distance the solve record wrote for it.

No line of this row puts the word `colormap` in front of a map's name, so no link into the explorer is derived from it and that refusal is the record's own. alt: A grid of twenty-four finished wallpapers from one curation pass, each labeled with the fractal family it was found in.
caption: Twenty-four of the seats one curation pass filled. With every rule applied, the gallery samples the range of the pool far more evenly than the judge's own top picks.
provenance: builder.picks — every panel is a seat of a recorded tentative gallery, named on this row by its own `<stamp>|<recipe key>` and resolved from artifacts/curation/tentative/<stamp>/gallery.jsonl for the seat and the candidate ledger for the recipe. Rendered fresh through the engine at 1280x720, supersample 3, then fitted to 205x115 and landed one file a panel, this figure being split rather than composited; the stored 640x360 thumbnail a seat points at is the picture the judges were shown and is not a source here. Nothing about the coloring is this figure's choice: mode, mode settings, curve, map, the whole palette pass and the cap all come off the ledger's recipe, except the map of a panel whose line says it was recolored. Stamp 20260902T164622Z; panels in reading order, 6 across.

Autolevel: every candidate behind these seats was made with band_autolevel/v1 switched on. A ledger recipe keeps only the reduced stamp of that — the operator, the switch and the band's sha256 — so the curve is read from the run's own record instead, depth/breadth_strange, depth/dc2, depth/empty_modes, depth/overnight_a_main, depth/overnight_b_main, depth/overnight_c_main, depth/sm_field, depth/smooth500_leg, depth/smooth500_pilot, depth/teal_conditioned, reframe_draw/q4_1h, runs/gallery2, runs/gallery4. The operator acted on 7d80ef09 (black point 0.1430, white point 0.7891), 23c51575 (black point 0.0000, white point 0.9957), and those panels were drawn through the stops that curve rebuilds — the wallpaper project's own `stops_from_stamp` replaying its own curve, never a second one measured here. It left the rest exactly alone, and those are the engine's own render. Held to that: each pick redrawn at the candidate's own 640x360 supersample 2 reproduces the stored picture its seat points at to mean absolute difference 3.0-5.5 of 255, codec floor 1.4-2.8, and `builder check`'s `seats` is what keeps it true.

Which seats stand for the pass is a seeded shuffle of its whole seating — scratch/curation/pick_output.py, seed 20260903 — taking the first that clear four rejections: a seat another figure already stands on, by key and by frame; a seat whose run recorded that the autolevel operator acted without recording the curve; and the caps that keep one draw from being a picture of itself rather than of the pass — at most four tiles of one rendering mode, three of one hue family, four of one partition. Nothing here was chosen for how it looks.
The spread that came back: eleven of the pass's fourteen modes, nine partitions, and all twelve hue families plus one picture the reading finds dominant in no color at all.

The pool solve.pool() offers: 518,436 candidates over 55,823 locations, 19,197 of them clearing the bar, pool stamp e0cf00ba4d14ca86.

The counts, as drawn: about 570,000 places walked; about 81,000 locations; about 570,000 candidates mined; about 520,000 candidates, 19,000 passing the judges; 1,000 seats in the general gallery, 8,000 across the 19 collections. Unrounded: 568,129 frames evaluated over 86 walk ledgers, 80,717 locations in their admitted union (next door's supply.ledgers.admitted_union); 566920 candidate-ledger rows (data/curation/candidate_ledger/rows.manifest.json); 518,436 in the pool solve.pool() offers and 19,197 of them clearing the fine bar; 1,000 seats in the general record 20260922T012627Z, 8,000 across 19 kept collection records (5,959 distinct candidates).

Which four places is a seeded shuffle of the general gallery's seats (seed 20260925), taking the first that clear one spread rule and three refusals. The spread: no two share a partition, a rendering mode or a main hue. The refusals: a seat at a location another figure already stands on, a seat or candidate whose run recorded that the autolevel operator acted without recording the curve, and a place where no other candidate in another mode was scored by the gallery judge. The middle stage's picture at a place is the best-scoring such candidate. Chosen by the session on Matt's instruction, for him to swap later; nothing here was chosen for how it looks.

Stage 1 draws each place from its seat's own ledger frame at 205x115, supersample 3, mode smooth, colormap twilight_shifted, cap from the depth-aware policy. Stages 2 and 3 are drawn from ledger recipes through the engine at 1280x720, supersample 3, then fitted to the tile.

Autolevel: every candidate behind these seats was made with band_autolevel/v1 switched on. A ledger recipe keeps only the reduced stamp of that — the operator, the switch and the band's sha256 — so the curve is read from the run's own record instead, depth/ame_c_deep, depth/armA_places_0906, depth/u3_dearrest_night2, rotation/ckpt120, runs/gallery4. It acted on none of them, which by that operator's rule means it returned each base render untouched, so every panel here is the engine's own render of the recipe. Held to that: each pick redrawn at the candidate's own 640x360 supersample 2 reproduces the stored picture its seat points at to mean absolute difference 3.0-5.5 of 255, codec floor 1.4-2.8, and `builder check`'s `seats` is what keeps it true.

provenance: builder.picks — every panel is a seat of a recorded tentative gallery, named on this row by its own `<stamp>|<recipe key>` and resolved from artifacts/curation/tentative/<stamp>/gallery.jsonl for the seat and the candidate ledger for the recipe. Rendered fresh through the engine at 1280x720, supersample 3, then fitted to 1292x727 and landed one file a panel, this figure being split rather than composited; the stored 640x360 thumbnail a seat points at is the picture the judges were shown and is not a source here. Nothing about the coloring is this figure's choice: mode, mode settings, curve, map, the whole palette pass and the cap all come off the ledger's recipe. Stamp 20260922T014052Z; panels in reading order, 1 across.

Autolevel: every candidate behind these seats was made with band_autolevel/v1 switched on. A ledger recipe keeps only the reduced stamp of that — the operator, the switch and the band's sha256 — so the curve is read from the run's own record instead, depth/on125_recolour2. It acted on none of them, which by that operator's rule means it returned each base render untouched, so every panel here is the engine's own render of the recipe. Held to that: each pick redrawn at the candidate's own 640x360 supersample 2 reproduces the stored picture its seat points at to mean absolute difference 3.0-5.5 of 255, codec floor 1.4-2.8, and `builder check`'s `seats` is what keeps it true.

Which seat is the icon's: Matt picked the icon off a contact sheet of forty square crops (favicon_sheet_ckpt145, F08), and this is the seat that crop was taken from, at its own whole frame. builder.icons holds the crop, and its row in article/figure-recipes.jsonl names this same seat.

provenance: builder.start:modes — 2 rows of 5 panels at 248x140, landed one file a panel. Which locations and candidates: Matt picked both rows off a contact sheet of 30 (start_modes_sheet_ckpt147). The sheet's rows were every location a kept record seats (the twenty final139_* solves and final140_general2000), less any place or seat key another figure already stood on, that the candidate ledger drew in all four modes; per mode the candidate with the best fine-head p_fine(>=4) from pool_scores.jsonl whose recipe frame is the location's own and whose tone curve is on its run's record, by scratch/start_modes_sheet/pick.py. Thirty locations cleared that, and the sheet showed all of them.
